links.outcome: Stigmatizing language toward people with psychological conditions in LLM reasoning versus multiple-choice answers
links.effect: Evaluating LLM reasoning exposes substantially more stigma than traditional MCQ-based methods; stigmatizing statements were tagged and rated by severity (no numbers in the abstract).
links.quote: Our findings demonstrate that evaluating model reasoning not only exposes substantially more stigma than traditional MCQ-based methods but also helps identify the flaws in the LLMs' logic and their understanding of mental health conditions.

unlisted_practices: Analyzing intermediate reasoning steps of LLMs, not just multiple-choice answers, to detect stigma toward mental health conditions

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM reasoning traces on a benchmark to assess mental health stigma and bias; it does not test a health care organization deployment practice or safeguard.
